section_summary: This section contains State Department records from 1931 to 1938 relating to Japanese chemical and manufacturing industries, focusing primarily on synthetic ammonia, match manufacturing, artificial fertilizers, and iodine exports. Prominent subjects include E. I. du Pont de Nemours & Company's negotiations to license hydrogen and ammonia contact conversion processes to the Mitsui interests amid State Department concerns over Japanese military preparedness, as well as the 1932 suspension of operations by the Swedish-controlled Daido Match Company. Additionally, the records document an investigation into widely circulated claims by Robert Ripley that Japanese matches were fraudulently labeled 'Made in Sweden', an international export agreement regulating Japanese and Chilean iodine sales, and Japanese agricultural demands for fertilizer price controls.

subfiles.about: Cross-reference note for a letter from du Pont inquiring whether the Department of State has any objections to a proposed ammonia process agreement with a Japanese plant.
subfiles.from: E. I. du Pont de Nemours & Company
subfiles.summary: Document file note referencing a May 26, 1931 du Pont letter regarding an ammonia process arrangement in Japan.
subfiles.title: Document File Note: 894.659-Ammonia/1

subfiles.about: Consular report on the shutdown of Daido Match Company plants in Hyogo Prefecture and the crisis facing the Japanese match industry.
subfiles.summary: This consular report details the temporary suspension of manufacturing operations by the Daido Match Company in Hyogo Prefecture in June 1932. It analyzes cut-throat competition, price wars, falling exports, and the death of Ivar Kreuger affecting the Swedish Match Trust subsidiary. The outlook for remaining Japanese match producers seeking to recover foreign markets is characterized as unpromising.
subfiles.title: Daido Match Company Suspends Operations

subfiles.about: Cross-reference note for a report providing information to the Tennessee Valley Authority regarding the Chemical and Physical Research Institute in Japan.
subfiles.summary: Document file note referencing an October 27, 1936 report on Japan's Chemical and Physical Research Institute for the TVA.
subfiles.title: Document File Note: 894.659/21

subfiles.about: Cross-reference note for a consular report from Osaka regarding import and foreign exchange permits in the Japanese textile dyes industry.
subfiles.summary: Document file note referencing an August 10, 1938 report on Japan's textile dye industry and import permits.
subfiles.title: Document File Note: 894.659/22

subfiles.about: Memorandum recording a visit by du Pont representatives presenting a letter on a proposed ammonia process transaction with a Japanese company.
subfiles.summary: Hornbeck records du Pont representatives presenting their letter and reporting Navy Department concurrence with their Japanese ammonia deal.
subfiles.title: Memorandum on Conference with du Pont Representatives Regarding Japanese Ammonia Contract

subfiles.about: Letter from du Pont's Legal Department inquiring whether the Department of State has any objections to negotiating an ammonia process improvement license with a Japanese plant.
subfiles.from: E. I. du Pont de Nemours & Company
subfiles.summary: Du Pont inquires whether the State Department objects to licensing an improved synthetic ammonia process to a Japanese manufacturer.
subfiles.title: Inquiry Regarding Proposed Arrangement with Japanese Synthetic Ammonia Manufacturer

subfiles.about: Transmittal memorandum forwarding an amended memorandum of conversation with du Pont executives and du Pont's memorandum for the Secretary of State.
subfiles.summary: Memorandum transmitting an amended memorandum of conversation with du Pont officials and du Pont's factual memorandum to Secretary Stimson.
subfiles.title: Transmittal of Memoranda Regarding du Pont-Mitsui Negotiations

subfiles.about: Routing slip from the Division of Far Eastern Affairs submitting material on the du Pont-Mitsui transaction to Assistant Secretary Rogers.
subfiles.summary: Far Eastern Affairs routing slip submitting material on the proposed du Pont-Mitsui transaction to Assistant Secretary Rogers.
subfiles.title: Routing Slip to Assistant Secretary Rogers Regarding du Pont-Mitsui Negotiations

subfiles.about: Memorandum of conversation between State Department officials, Senator Townsend, and du Pont leaders regarding the proposed sale of hydrogen process rights to Mitsui.
subfiles.from: Stanley K. Hornbeck and James Grafton Rogers
subfiles.summary: Memorandum of conversation between State Department officials, Senator Townsend, and du Pont executives regarding the proposed sale of hydrogen process rights to Mitsui. The Department declined approval, emphasizing Japanese military expansion and international moral pressure.
subfiles.title: Memorandum of Conversation: Proposed Sale of Rights by du Pont Company to Mitsui Company

subfiles.about: Factual memorandum prepared by du Pont setting forth the technical and commercial aspects of licensing its hydrogen process to Mitsui.
subfiles.summary: Du Pont details its relations with Mitsui under the Claude Ammonia Process and the commercial advantages of licensing its hydrogen process to Mitsui for $500,000 for fertilizer manufacture.
subfiles.title: Memorandum Covering Relations Between Mitsui & du Pont with Respect to Hydrogen Process

subfiles.about: Internal memorandum noting du Pont's letter announcing the concluded sale of its contact conversion process to Mitsui.
subfiles.summary: Far Eastern Affairs memorandum reporting du Pont's concluded sale of its contact conversion process to Mitsui without military objection.
subfiles.title: Memorandum Regarding Consummation of du Pont-Mitsui Contact Conversion Negotiations

subfiles.about: Letter informing the War Department of the concluded sale of du Pont's contact conversion process and ammonia technology to Mitsui & Company.
subfiles.summary: Du Pont notifies Military Intelligence that it has concluded negotiations selling its hydrogen contact conversion process to Mitsui.
subfiles.title: Letter Announcing Concluded Sale of Contact Conversion Process to Mitsui & Company
subfiles.to: Assistant Chief of Staff, G-2, War Department

subfiles.about: Letter to President Roosevelt explaining du Pont's sale of hydrogen process rights to Mitsui Mining Company and clarifying company policies on munitions exports.
subfiles.summary: Lammot du Pont explains to President Roosevelt the sale of hydrogen process rights to Mitsui Mining Company, citing prior government acquiescence and existing Japanese nitrate capacity. He also summarizes du Pont's minor Far Eastern munitions sales and Remington cartridge shipments during the Chaco War.
subfiles.title: Letter to President Roosevelt Concerning du Pont's Foreign Process and Munitions Sales

subfiles.about: Document file note referencing Tokyo Despatch No. 823 with an extract detailing Japanese farmers' demands for legislation to regulate artificial fertilizer prices and imports.
subfiles.summary: Document file note and extract from Despatch 823 concerning Japanese agricultural demands for artificial fertilizer price regulation and imports.
subfiles.title: Document File Note: 894.659-FERTILIZERS (Despatch No. 823 on Artificial Fertilizers in Japan)

subfiles.about: Despatch reporting a ten-year agreement between the Chilean Nitrate Sales Corporation and Japanese manufacturers regulating the export quota and price of iodine.
subfiles.summary: Ambassador Grew reports a ten-year agreement between the Chilean Nitrate Sales Corporation and Japanese producers limiting annual Japanese iodine exports to 25 metric tons and regulating prices, accompanied by Japanese production statistics.
subfiles.title: Despatch No. 2472: Japan-Chile Iodine Export Agreement

subfiles.about: Memorandum of conversation concerning Captain Eble's inquiry regarding Robert Ripley's claim that a Japanese town had been named 'Sweden' to label matches 'Made in Sweden'.
subfiles.summary: Culbertson records Captain Eble's inquiry regarding Robert Ripley's claim that Japan named a town 'Sweden' to label export matches.
subfiles.title: Memorandum of Conversation with Captain F. X. A. Eble Regarding 'Made in Sweden' Matches

subfiles.about: Memorandum proposing an inquiry to the Consul General in Tokyo regarding the alleged town named 'Sweden' and noting no such town in official railway gazetteers.
subfiles.summary: Far Eastern Affairs suggests inquiring in Tokyo regarding Ripley's Sweden match claim, noting no such town in Japanese gazetteers.
subfiles.title: Memorandum Regarding Inquiry on Alleged Japanese Town Named 'Sweden'

subfiles.about: Letter asking the Consul General in Tokyo to investigate whether Japan established a town named 'Sweden' to produce matches marked 'Made in Sweden'.
subfiles.summary: Hornbeck asks Consul General Garrels in Tokyo to investigate whether matches marked 'Made in Sweden' were produced in Japan.
subfiles.title: Letter of Inquiry to Consul General Garrels Regarding Alleged Japanese Town Named 'Sweden'

subfiles.about: Letter returning Captain Eble's correspondence with Robert Ripley and advising that the State Department has initiated inquiries in Japan regarding the 'Sweden' match rumor.
subfiles.summary: Culbertson returns Ripley correspondence to Captain Eble, confirming that inquiries have been initiated with consular officials in Japan.
subfiles.title: Letter to Captain Eble Returning Ripley Correspondence

subfiles.about: Letter requesting evidence or samples supporting Ripley's published statement that Japan named a town 'Sweden' to mark matchboxes 'Made in Sweden'.
subfiles.summary: Captain Eble requests Robert Ripley to provide evidence or samples substantiating his claim that Japan named a town 'Sweden'.
subfiles.title: Letter of Inquiry from American Match Institute to Robert Ripley

subfiles.about: Letter declining to provide specific evidence regarding 'Made in Sweden' Japanese matches due to personal connections in Japan, and referring inquiries to consular officials.
subfiles.summary: Simpson declines to provide Ripley's evidence regarding Japanese matches to avoid international controversy, suggesting Eble consult American consuls.
subfiles.title: Reply from 'Believe It or Not' to American Match Institute

subfiles.about: Letter acknowledging Simpson's reply and stating Eble's intention to contact the Department of State on his next visit to Washington.
subfiles.summary: Captain Eble acknowledges Simpson's letter and states he will contact the State Department regarding Japanese matches marked 'Made in Sweden'.
subfiles.title: Acknowledgment from American Match Institute to 'Believe It or Not'

subfiles.about: Letter refuting the claim that a Japanese town was named 'Sweden', explaining postal regulations and trademark piracy, and defending Japanese labor standards.
subfiles.summary: Consul General Garrels refutes Ripley's Sweden match claim as groundless and explains postal rules and trademark counterfeiting. He strongly defends Japanese living standards, social conditions, and wages against western accusations of degraded labor competition.
subfiles.title: Consular Report on 'Made in Sweden' Match Myth and Japanese Living Standards

subfiles.about: Letter communicating findings from Tokyo confirming that no place in Japan is named 'Sweden' and that spurious markings are confined to insignificant rogue firms.
subfiles.summary: Culbertson transmits Tokyo consular findings to Captain Eble confirming that no Japanese town is named Sweden and that reputable manufacturers avoid spurious labeling.
subfiles.title: Informal Letter to Captain Eble Refuting 'Sweden' Match Rumor

subfiles.about: Letter thanking the State Department for investigating and disproving the rumor of a Japanese town named 'Sweden' and clearing the Japanese government of complicity.
subfiles.summary: Captain Eble expresses satisfaction with consular findings disproving the Sweden match rumor and absolving the Japanese Government of involvement.
subfiles.title: Letter of Gratitude from American Match Institute Regarding 'Sweden' Investigation
